transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm really only here because my family and our parish priest insisted I come, but I don't think I need to be. My family keeps saying my beliefs about the festival and people watching me aren’t real, but I know they’re true and I can’t be convinced otherwise. They are the ones who are mistaken, not me.
Have you experienced any distinct periods where your mood was exceptionally elevated, or conversely, where you felt significantly depressed or hopeless for weeks at a time?

Yes, I swing from feeling on top of the world with my big plans for the festival to crashing into a heavy, guilty sadness where I feel hopeless and wonder what the point of me being here is. Those low, heavy feelings have been creeping in on and off for most of the past year, but these intense highs and crashing lows have really taken over during the last two months.
During the last two months when you were experiencing these intense mood swings, were your delusions about the festival present even when your mood was stable and not high or low?

No, those beliefs and the voice only happen when I am really revved up and energized with the festival plans. When my mood is normal or stable, I don't experience those things at all. It only happens when I am in that high state.
When you feel those 'crashed' or depressed moods, do you experience any of those same beliefs or hear the voice, or do those symptoms only occur when your mood is high?

No, those things never happen when I am feeling down or depressed. The voice and the beliefs about being watched only come on when I'm highly energized and working on my festival plans. When I'm in those heavy, sad periods, those experiences completely disappear.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates included F30.2 (Manic episode with psychotic symptoms) and F31.5 (Bipolar disorder, current episode depressed with psychotic symptoms), but the patient explicitly stated that the psychotic symptoms (delusions/hallucinations) occur ONLY during the elevated/manic mood states and are absent during depressed or euthymic states. This clinical presentation is most consistent with F31.2 (Bipolar disorder, current episode manic with psychotic symptoms), as the psychotic features are mood-congruent and limited to the manic episodes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits clear manic episodes characterized by grandiose delusions and auditory hallucinations, alternating with depressive episodes. Crucially, the psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during the mood-elevated (manic) phase and are absent during euthymic or depressive periods, which is diagnostic of Bipolar I Disorder with psychotic features.
